cells.tense: You are holding what's true and adjusting the blend as you go.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Lay out for the people it touches how the thing is arranged and how you read it — plainly, out loud — then leave it standing there for a day without arguing anyone into it.
cells.core:
You hold more of what's true here than you show, and you keep the blending going as you go — adding a little, holding some back, keeping the proportions right. That is why someone can walk in carrying a mess and leave steadied, without either of you naming what just happened.

The share you haven't taken is the saying. Put the frame on the table before you're asked: how the thing is arranged, how you read it, plainly — then leave it lying there for a day and don't argue it into place. The people around it get something they can point at and use. You stop being the only one holding the whole arrangement, and anything built next stands on ground you and they can both see.
cells.sheetLine: They already feel it. Say how it's arranged.
cells.verb: Holding many true things at once and knowing each of them by name
cells.place: Where what's added, held back and blended is adjusted as it goes

cells.tense: You will have every branch of it mapped, and you're steering by all of them at once.
cells.act: turn toward the one direction and stop surveying
cells.ask: Pick one direction that's yours to want and walk it three days without opening the others while you're on it.
cells.core:
There's so much available here that every direction stays live, and surveying starts standing in for choosing. You're not confused — you have more detail than anyone at the table asked for, and the readiness is steady enough that it just keeps adding. Meanwhile the thing you'd steer by sits unwalked, and the ones around you are getting the survey instead of you.

One heading, held and attuned, is the correction — not more information. Pick the direction you want and keep it three days. You'll still have everything you knew. The difference is that this one thing gets to meet you rather than the whole view, and whatever is genuinely developing gets room to reach an end. What shines does so because it was carried through, not scouted.

cells.tense: You were in the middle of something that mattered, and you've stepped out of it.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Ask someone who matters to do the next piece of something beside you — same hands, same hour, no briefing.
cells.core:
You read people well, and little has been going back in when you do it. You notice the exchange sitting low, keep seeing it, keep deciding it isn't the hour. Pushing on that directly comes back empty, which is why effort aimed at it hasn't worked and won't.

Go at it from the other side. Choose someone who matters and do the next piece of something beside them — same hands, same hour, no briefing. Not because the pair will finish it, but because working in step puts you back into what you read so well: it arrives through doing-with, not through trying. After a stretch the reading comes back without being chased; it was waiting for you to be present where the work is.

cells.tense: You already know what's fair here, and you haven't said whose knowing it is.
cells.act: return the small thing you owe before anyone asks
cells.ask: Settle what you owe — a reply, a return, a kept word — before anyone has to come asking, and no explaining after.
cells.core:
You've been doing the adjuster's work — sensing where the weight sits, easing the blend — as though it were simply how things are. Anyone watching could describe the fairness you keep: what's owed, to whom, in what measure. Your own account of these months leaves that scale out, and the scale stays accurate whether or not you sign it.

Settle what you owe before anyone has to ask — a reply owed, something borrowed, a word you gave — and no explaining afterward. Returning it closes the gap and names the holder in the same motion. The compass reading you've been acting on is yours to own; it has been keeping the books while you looked somewhere else.
cells.sheetLine: The scale is accurate. Sign it.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: that this person's perceptions are landing without argument when the fullness sits at Tune — a Bound signature holding myriads in a seat built for continuous adjusting — the record only gives the capacity and the seat, not their history. The reader could say 'I do argue, I fight about it' — so every cell describes the mechanism in a moment they could recognize, never a motive. The asks survive a wrong read: each is one small visible act (a standing thing said plainly, one direction kept three days, one shared piece of work, one small debt paid) that teaches something even if the picture misses. The sentence that serves me more than them: 'you hold many truths at once' — it is pretty; it comes out, because a person holding many truths may simply be tired.
